stem: Worker A can complete a job in 10 days. Worker B can complete the same job in 15 days. Working together, how many days will they take to finish the job?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Student averages the two times: (10+15)/2 = 12.5, then rounds to 8, or uses harmonic average incorrectly as (10+15)/2 = 12.5 approximately 8.
Student computes 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/5 (wrong: 2/20 + 1/20 = 3/20 is not 1/5), or simplifies 5/30 to 1/5 instead of 1/6, giving 5 days.
Student adds the two times directly: 10 + 15 = 25 days, confusing sum of times with combined work.

explanation: When two workers have individual rates 1/10 and 1/15 of the job per day, their combined rate is the sum: 1/10 + 1/15 = 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6 job per day. Time to complete the job together = 1 / (1/6) = 6 days.

explanation_sections.punchline: Add work rates: 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6 job/day, so time = 6 days.
explanation_sections.approach: Convert each worker's time to a daily rate (fraction of job per day). Add the rates to get the combined rate. Take the reciprocal for the combined time.
explanation_sections.lesson: Work rates add, not times. Never add times directly.
explanation_sections.timing: Under 45 seconds. The LCM of 10 and 15 is 30; finding 3/30 + 2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6 is fast. The trap is option 4 (25 days) from adding times.
